blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Global environmental governance should be reformed by reducing fragmentation of the agencies concerned and ensuring that developing nations receive adequate resources to fulfill international commitments. Secretary Juan Miguel “Mitch” T. Cuna of the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) stressed this point in his address on Wednesday at the high-level political dialogue on “Renewing Environmental Multilateralism” at the 81st United Nations General Assembly (UNGA 81) in New York City. The dialogue, which was hosted by the governments of Panama and Vanuatu, aims to adapt international cooperation amid growing geopolitical complexity and institutional pressures.
